title: CAP-GATE-POSTHOC: would a CAPABILITY split gate accept the sites the geometric gate certifies? (zero judge calls, zero constructions; EXPLORATORY feasibility study before any capability-gated construction)
question: The construction accepts a split on geometry and certifies a site afterwards against its own 300-rep site null. A capability gate would accept a split only when the children carry different model-performance profiles (key-only LOO Brier gain of the children over the parent, in-roster and LOMO). Do the two gates accept the same sites, a subset, or different ones, and how many sites clear BOTH? Primary object the af tree (69 sites, 16 certified); abt2, bareq512, the promoted bareq512_s42 and o0 beside.

sentence_of_record: CAP-GATE-POSTHOC (2026-09-17, zero calls; af tree 69 sites / 16 certified on 5,602 train-side keyed questions, pool of record scored nowhere): the capability gate at t=+1.0 accepts 24 sites of which 9 are certified (7 certified-only, 15 accepted-only, Jaccard 0.29), a DIFFERENT SET from the geometric certificate at every registered threshold, a superset of it only against each site's own null median (16/16 certified clear, 38 accepted-only); the falsifier did not fire (joint 9 not < 8; certified-uncertified +1.20 not < +0.5) and P3 (>= 11) failed, so the outcome lies in the gap between the two registered branches; builder's P1, P2, P3, P5, P8, P9 FAILED, P4, P7, P10 HELD, P6 PARTLY; orchestrator's P1 HELD, P3 FAILED. Caveats of record: the t=0 line is not a zero line (within-site null LOMO -0.54/1000 at the median site, -0.93 below n=150, Spearman with n +0.89), which halves rho(n) (+0.35 -> +0.16), removes rho(depth) (-0.28 -> -0.07), and reduces the P7 depth contrast to +0.50 and the P10 certified contrast to +0.43; the certified contrast is mostly size (matched on log n +0.31, partial rho +0.05); on the tree's own held-out side minus the pool of record (2,193 q, median 79 per site) the median is +0.45, rho with the train-side gain +0.21, joint at t=+1 6/16 and the certified contrast +0.34, both falsifier legs met at low power, the trunk (root, both depth-1 sites, n00000163) replicating and the two strongest depth-4 sites flipping sign; P5's -5.18 is median/median with the in-roster median at -0.10 and is uninterpretable, and g_in - g_lomo (negative at 52/69 sites) is the differential LOO penalty, not a roster-specific residual. Reading: geometric certification is sufficient for capability content only above the site's own null and never necessary; a capability gate would be an additive second admission rule, and the 'different sites' case rests on small, deep sites whose gains do not replicate out of sample. plain_description.what: On an existing tree (69 split points, 16 of which are statistically certified on geometry), checks whether a 'capability' rule would accept the same splits. That rule keeps a split only if the child cells really show different model-performance profiles. No new judge calls and no new tree builds.
plain_description.why: Statistical separation in embedding space does not automatically mean the cells differ in what models can do. This tests whether the certificate has capability meaning.
plain_description.information: If the two rules picked the same splits, geometry would be a stand-in for capability; if they picked different ones, the two notions come apart. Result (exploratory): mostly different sets. At the main threshold the capability rule accepts 24 splits, 9 of them certified; overlap is low (about 0.29). The certified splits clear the capability rule only when each is compared with its own random baseline. On held-out data the top-level splits replicate, but the two strongest deep splits flip sign. Reading: geometric certification is enough for capability content only above the split's own baseline, and it is never necessary.
